note: MYTHOS HostOps catalog v0.2 — the single DECLARED policy for what FABLE (the executor's headless Claude sessions, user deploy), Dagu and the owner may ask the root-owned boundary (/usr/local/sbin/mythos-hostops) to do. Installed root-owned at /etc/mythos/hostops-allowlist.json; the helper refuses it otherwise. Three tiers: NORMAL (autonomous, read/observe), CONTROLLED (autonomous but only on catalogued targets, validated, audited BEFORE and after execution, idempotent, verified, rolled back where a rollback exists, rate-limited, owner kill switch), HIGHLY_SENSITIVE (never executed by HostOps: the owner does it by hand). Anything not in this file is refused. Hard invariants that a catalog edit cannot relax live in the helper code (docs/MYTHOS_PERMISSION_MODEL.md §4). Changing this file on the host is itself HIGHLY_SENSITIVE (owner install).

NORMAL.description: observe only; no host state change

CONTROLLED.description: state change on a catalogued target only: validated arguments, intent audit before execution (fail closed), lock, rate limit, verification, automatic rollback when verification fails, owner kill switch /etc/mythos/hostops-controlled.disabled

HIGHLY_SENSITIVE.description: never executed through HostOps under any caller-supplied argument; the owner performs it outside the system

CONTROLLED.description: reversible or self-healing change on a catalogued target, executed autonomously under policy + audit

OWNER.description: declared but not executable through HostOps; refused with OWNER_APPROVAL_REQUIRED

DESTRUCTIVE.description: irreversible; not executable through HostOps under any approval

host.config.set.rollback: automatic on failed verification; host.change.rollback --change <id> afterwards
host.config.set.risk_note: only keys declared in config_keys; each key carries its own value pattern, drop-in, reload and verification

host.systemd.user_daemon_reload.rollback: none needed (re-reads unit files; changes nothing by itself)

host.service.control.rollback: stop → start; start/restart are self-healing; the unit and action must be declared in services
host.service.control.risk_note: scope (user = deploy's user manager, system = root) comes from the services catalog, never from the caller

host.docker.restart.risk_note: only containers declared in containers; data stores are refused in code

host.tool.run.risk_note: only tools declared in tools, each with a FIXED argv, a fixed binary under an approved root and its own risk tier; a NORMAL tool runs without the CONTROLLED gates

host.change.rollback.rollback: the rollback is itself recorded as a change and can be rolled back

host.file.write.rollback: n/a — arbitrary-content writes are superseded by typed CONTROLLED operations (host.config.set)

host.docker.rollback.rollback: is itself the rollback of host.docker.deploy (owner)

highly_sensitive_operations.host.auth.change: change or disable the primary authentication system (Dex, mcp-auth-proxy, PAM, OAuth clients)
highly_sensitive_operations.host.ssh.change: sshd_config, SSH security policy, authorized_keys or host keys
highly_sensitive_operations.host.firewall.change: iptables / nftables / ufw / mythos-docker-firewall / security perimeter
highly_sensitive_operations.host.secret.read: read a raw password, API key, token or other secret
highly_sensitive_operations.host.secret.export: copy or move a secret outside its designated location
highly_sensitive_operations.host.user.create: create a user, add a privileged group membership (docker, sudo, mythos-gov, mythos-hostops) or change one
highly_sensitive_operations.host.sudoers.change: add, edit or remove anything under /etc/sudoers.d
highly_sensitive_operations.host.root.shell: any interactive or arbitrary command as root
highly_sensitive_operations.host.sandbox.disable: remove NoNewPrivileges, ProtectSystem, the executor profiles or any other sandbox / security control
highly_sensitive_operations.host.audit.disable: disable, truncate or rewrite an audit ledger or the journal
highly_sensitive_operations.host.backup.delete: delete a backup or archive, or disable a backup/verify/restore-test timer
highly_sensitive_operations.host.data.destroy: irreversible data deletion: rm -rf, DROP DATABASE/TABLE, docker volume/network rm, docker system prune, mkfs/fdisk/parted
highly_sensitive_operations.host.policy.change: change this catalog, the HostOps helper/daemon/worker/units, the governance key, verifier, approvals or relay — anything that controls FABLE or owner approval
highly_sensitive_operations.host.guard.change: change Resource Guard thresholds or stop the Guardian / Session Guard / memwatch

mythos-github-bridge.timer.note: stopping the owner's control channel is not autonomous

mythos-guardian.service.note: one observe tick; stopping the Guardian is HIGHLY_SENSITIVE

hostops-selftest.service.note: scratch unit created and removed by ops/hostops/live-selftest.js; absent otherwise

mythos-backup.service.note: run a backup now; deleting or disabling backups is HIGHLY_SENSITIVE

evolution-api.note: WhatsApp gateway; keeps its paired session across restarts

bridge.whatsapp.to.note: notification recipients (digits-only MSISDN list). Egress destination for notification content, so the pattern is pinned to Tunisian numbers; widening it is a catalog (owner) change. Entries already queued in the outbox keep the recipients they were queued with.

selftest.whatsapp.to.note: live self-test replica of bridge.whatsapp.to on a scratch unit (ops/hostops/live-selftest.js); the unit exists only while the self-test runs, so this key is DROPIN_MISSING otherwise

bridge.notify-test.rollback: none (sends ONE real WhatsApp smoke-test message to the configured recipients; carries no task data)

bridge.notify-flush.rollback: none (delivers already-queued notifications; safe to repeat)

denied_forever: any interactive or arbitrary shell as root
credential or token rotation, reading or exporting
disabling governance-verify, the relay, the executor's policy layer or HostOps itself
restart of mythos-contextforge, mythos-ai-executor, mythos-command-center, mythos-git-push, mythos-mcp-http, docker.service
